The AI Engineer internship in short

In the SkillMe AI Engineer internship you build TicketPilot: Support Ticket Triage Agent, a project where you build an AI agent that reads incoming support tickets, calls tools to look up real information, and decides what to do next — then prove it actually works with evals. In week 1 you get a free LLM API key and make your first tool-calling request: instead of just replying with text, the model decides to call a Python function you defined. By week 4 you wrap the triage agent in a small API, write an evaluation set to measure how often it triages correctly, and add guardrails so it fails safely. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

Week by week

What each week of the AI Engineer internship covers

The four milestones of TicketPilot: Support Ticket Triage Agent.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Your First Tool-Calling LLM Call

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Get a free LLM API key and make your first tool-calling request: instead of just replying with text, the model decides to call a Python function you defined. This is the core mechanic every agent in this track builds on.

    What you learn

    • Getting and using a free-tier LLM API key with tool/function-calling support (Google Gemini API or Groq)
    • Defining a tool schema (name, description, parameters) that the model can call
    • Reading a tool-call response and executing the matching Python function
    • Sending the tool's result back to the model for a final answer

    What you submit

    • A working lookup_order_status tool function with sample data
    • A tool schema definition wired into a chat completion request
    • Glue code that executes a model-requested tool call and returns the result
    • A README explaining the tool-calling flow end to end
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • Asking about a known order ID returns a correct, tool-grounded answer, not a guess
    • Asking about an unknown order ID makes the tool return 'not found' and the model reports that honestly
    • The API key never appears anywhere in committed code or Git history
    • Printing the raw API response shows a clear tool-call step before the final answer

    Stretch goal: Add a second tool, lookup_customer(email: str), and see if the model can chain both tools in one conversation to answer a two-part question.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Multi-Tool Triage Agent

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn last week's single tool call into a real triage agent that reads a support ticket, classifies it, and calls the right combination of tools to gather context before drafting a reply. This is where 'an LLM that can call one function' becomes 'an agent that reasons about which tools to use.'

    What you learn

    • Designing a small toolset for one workflow (lookup, classify, escalate)
    • Writing a system prompt that defines an agent's role, tools, and boundaries
    • Handling a multi-turn tool-calling loop where the model can call more than one tool per ticket
    • Structuring ticket data and agent output for a real workflow

    What you submit

    • A tickets.json file with realistic sample tickets
    • Three working tools: order lookup, category classification, refund eligibility
    • A multi-round tool-calling loop with a max-rounds safety cap
    • A batch run over all sample tickets with printed categories, tool calls and drafted replies
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • Running the agent over all sample tickets produces a category and draft reply for each one
    • At least one ticket in the sample set requires the agent to call two different tools before replying
    • The safety cap is verified by testing with a deliberately confusing ticket and confirming the loop stops
    • A previously wrong category or tool choice is fixed and verified after a prompt or description tweak

    Stretch goal: Add an escalate_to_human(reason: str) tool the agent can call for tickets it isn't confident about, and track how often it gets used across your sample set.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    RAG for Policy-Grounded Replies

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Give the triage agent a company policy knowledge base so its drafted replies are grounded in real refund/shipping rules instead of the model's guesses. This combines retrieval-augmented generation with the tool-calling loop from Week 2 into one working agent.

    What you learn

    • Chunking and embedding a small internal knowledge base
    • Exposing retrieval as a callable tool (search_policy_docs) rather than a fixed pre-step
    • Combining RAG with tool-calling in a single agent loop
    • Grounding generated text in retrieved context and citing the source

    What you submit

    • 4-6 policy documents forming a small internal knowledge base
    • A search_policy_docs retrieval tool with cached embeddings
    • An updated agent that calls retrieval before drafting policy-related replies
    • Replies that show which policy chunk(s) grounded each claim
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • A refund-related ticket produces a reply that correctly cites a real rule from refund_policy.txt
    • A question about a policy not covered by any document gets an honest 'cannot confirm' response instead of a fabricated rule
    • Re-running the agent does not re-embed the policy documents from scratch (cache is used)
    • At least 3 sample tickets show retrieval being called before the reply is drafted

    Stretch goal: Add a top_k sensitivity test: compare retrieved chunks and reply quality at top_k=1 vs top_k=3 on 3 tricky tickets.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    API, Evals and Guardrails

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Wrap the triage agent in a small API, write an evaluation set to measure how often it triages correctly, and add guardrails so it fails safely. This is the engineering polish that turns a working prototype into something you could hand to another team.

    What you learn

    • Exposing an agent as an HTTP endpoint with a lightweight framework (FastAPI or Flask)
    • Writing an evaluation set with expected categories and required policy citations
    • Measuring agent accuracy and tool-call correctness against ground truth
    • Adding guardrails: input validation, rate limiting basics, and safe failure modes

    What you submit

    • A POST /triage API endpoint wrapping the full agent
    • Input validation and safe error handling on the endpoint
    • An eval_tickets.json set and evaluate.py script reporting accuracy
    • A guardrail that escalates low-confidence or under-grounded triage decisions
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • POST /triage with a real ticket body returns a category, reply and tool trace within a reasonable time
    • A deliberately malformed request (empty body) returns a clean error, not a crash
    • python evaluate.py runs at least 10 checks and reports an overall accuracy percentage
    • A ticket engineered to be low-confidence or ungrounded is escalated instead of answered with a guess

    Stretch goal: Add a /triage/batch endpoint that accepts a list of tickets and returns results with total latency and per-ticket timing, useful for a simple load check.

Is it for you?

Who the AI Engineer internship is for, and what you leave with

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of LLM APIs, RAG and Agents and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.
  • You can start at beginner level. Week 1: Get a free LLM API key and make your first tool-calling request: instead of just replying with text, the model decides to call a Python function you defined.
  • You want to reach intermediate+ level in four weeks. Week 4: Wrap the triage agent in a small API, write an evaluation set to measure how often it triages correctly, and add guardrails so it fails safely.
  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

AI Engineer internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the AI Engineer internship?

You build TicketPilot: Support Ticket Triage Agent. Build an AI agent that reads incoming support tickets, calls tools to look up real information, and decides what to do next — then prove it actually works with evals. It is one project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the AI Engineer internship?

The AI Engineer internship works with LLM APIs, RAG and Agents. Week 1: getting and using a free-tier LLM API key with tool/function-calling support (Google Gemini API or Groq); defining a tool schema (name, description, parameters) that the model can call. Week 2: designing a small toolset for one workflow (lookup, classify, escalate); writing a system prompt that defines an agent's role, tools, and boundaries. Week 3: chunking and embedding a small internal knowledge base; exposing retrieval as a callable tool (search_policy_docs) rather than a fixed pre-step. Week 4: exposing an agent as an HTTP endpoint with a lightweight framework (FastAPI or Flask); writing an evaluation set with expected categories and required policy citations.

Do I need experience to apply for the AI Engineer internship?

You need the basics of LLM APIs, RAG and Agents, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you get a free LLM API key and make your first tool-calling request: instead of just replying with text, the model decides to call a Python function you defined. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each AI Engineer milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of TicketPilot: Support Ticket Triage Agent, that means: asking about a known order ID returns a correct, tool-grounded answer, not a guess; asking about an unknown order ID makes the tool return 'not found' and the model reports that honestly; the API key never appears anywhere in committed code or Git history; printing the raw API response shows a clear tool-call step before the final answer. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the AI Engineer internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Made my first tool-calling LLM request where the model chose which function to run; Wired a Python function into an LLM agent's tool-calling loop end to end; Learned how tool schemas and tool responses fit into a real agent request; Built a multi-tool support ticket triage agent with a real tool-calling loop; Designed a toolset and system prompt so an LLM could gather context before replying; Added a safety cap to prevent runaway tool-calling loops in an autonomous agent; Built a policy knowledge base and exposed retrieval as a callable tool in an AI agent; Combined RAG with tool-calling so agent replies cite real, retrieved policy rules; Verified the agent gives an honest 'cannot confirm' answer instead of fabricating policy; Wrapped my AI triage agent in a FastAPI endpoint with input validation and error handling; Built an evaluation suite that measures triage accuracy against ground-truth tickets; Added a guardrail that escalates low-confidence tickets instead of letting the agent guess.

Is the AI Engineer internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based and goes to the interns whose reviewed AI Engineer work stands out in their cohort, not to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
